The three vectors share an origin, and each grid square has the same side length.

![](images/47/472d6130b8d885f7d053919197ccb8a2890ff142afa37c7f1741ae6826966039.png)

Given $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.
questions.:question/worked-solution:
First trace $2\mathbf{b}$ from the common origin $O$ to a point $P$: keep its direction and scale its length. The remaining path from $P$ to the endpoint $C$ must be the unknown multiple of $\mathbf{a}$.

![](images/ed/ed48daa17c0b9bd21a45911526e7d223438380df9dc41b6593de9bdd81538c43.png)

Following the grid direction of $\mathbf{a}$ takes $2$ steps, while the parallel path $PC$ has $6$ steps. Their length ratio is $\frac{6}{2}=3$. The remaining path points in the opposite direction to $\mathbf{a}$, so
$$
\overrightarrow{PC}=-3\mathbf{a}.
$$
Adding the path vectors gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c}&=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC}\\
&=2\mathbf{b}+(-3\mathbf{a})\\
&=-3\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Because $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are nonparallel, these coefficients are unique. Comparing with $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}$ gives $\lambda=-3$. The minus sign records the reversed direction.
